paragraphs: Thousands of firefighters across France and Spain are battling massive wildfires that have forced nearly 375,000 people to evacuate their homes. It is one of Europe’s largest evacuation efforts since World War II.

In southwestern France, blazes near Bordeaux have burned tens of thousands of hectares, destroyed property and left thick ash in the air. Meanwhile, thousands have been evacuated in Spain’s Valencia region. Supported by international aircraft and personnel, emergency crews worked around the clock during a brief period of cooler weather to contain the flames. However, many fires remain out of control, and forecasted heatwaves with temperatures up to 38°C threaten to intensify the crisis.

Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez blamed global warming for escalating disasters and called for national action to address climate emergencies. The damage is terrible, and politicians are already arguing, but local teams and helpful volunteers have managed to keep people safe so far.

paragraphs: Thousands of firefighters in France and Spain are fighting huge wildfires. More than 370,000 people had to leave their homes to stay safe during one of Europe’s largest evacuations.

In places like Bordeaux in France and Valencia in Spain, the fires burned thousands of hectares of land and destroyed many houses. Teams from other countries sent planes and helicopters to help drop water on the flames. Firefighters worked hard during cooler nights to control the blazes, but the situation is still dangerous.

Weather experts warn that a new heatwave with very high temperatures will arrive soon, which could make the fires worse. Luckily, no civilians died, but many families cannot return home yet and must stay in emergency shelters.

paragraphs: Big fires are burning forests and homes in France and Spain. Thousands of firefighters are working day and night to stop the flames. Many planes drop water from the sky.

Almost 370,000 people must leave their homes to stay safe. They are staying with friends or in special safe places. The air is full of smoke, and many houses are broken. Firefighters want to stop the fires fast because very hot weather is coming this week.

Hot weather makes fires grow big quickly. Nobody died in the fires, but people are worried and cannot go home now. Spanish officials say that climate change is the problem. They are arguing about what to do.
